title: darwin-memo: self-curating memory for LLM agents
description: Survival-selection memory for LLM agents. Lessons hold balances of a single conserved resource; a decide/settle/tick ledger credits and debits them from measured outcomes, charges upkeep, and buries entries that starve. No LLM judge is used in the mechanism, a design stance justified on cost and circularity grounds. This deposit archives the software together with the paper (paper/main.tex, "Attacking the Curator: Curation-Targeted Attacks on Agent Memory, and What Survives Them"), which defines the curation-targeted attack -- an adversary that corrupts the settlement signal rather than injecting poison -- and measures curation mechanisms against it across attack budgets and seeds, with exact paired permutation tests and Holm-Bonferroni correction. It reports negative results as prominently as positive ones: absent an attacker the mechanism buys leanness and cost, not accuracy, and on real coding tasks no memory arm beat no memory at all. Ships a frozen reproduction package (paper/reproduce.md, paper/reproduce.sh) whose per-seed result JSON is bound to a manifest and checked in CI, where tests re-derive the paper's printed numbers from that committed evidence. The superseded v0.5.1 technical report is kept under docs/research/.
